data.why: The repo bundles all datasets it needs under data/ (temperature, GHG, ice, ocean, energy, radiative-forcing CSVs/xlsx/nc); get_data.py reads these local files directly or as fallbacks when its live-URL fetches fail, so no uploads or synthetic files are required.

goals: Compare independent global temperature anomaly reconstructions (GISTEMP, HadCRUT, NOAA, Berkeley Earth) to check how well they agree
Trace CO2/CH4/N2O concentration histories from ice cores through modern instrumental records to contextualize the pace of current change
Quantify national and sectoral greenhouse-gas emission trends and compare them against mitigation pathway targets (Climate Action Tracker)
Examine sea-ice extent, land-ice mass and snow-cover trends by hemisphere and season to track cryosphere decline
Explore ocean heat content, sea-level rise and ocean pH time series to understand ocean-climate coupling
Inspect derived physical climate quantities (ECS, TCR, radiative forcing, climate feedbacks) underlying model projections

review.summary: The goal and phases describe a tool for putting current climate change in context across records and timescales, and every screen I opened (11) supports its node. It should be fixed before filing: the Maps page is absent, the Energy and Quantities pages are thin, it wrongly says no ocean heat content chart exists, and the features leave out the recurring chart displays.
